issue_ledger.exact_failure: validate_branch_bus_v251.py parses reports with Python json.loads and derives both deterministic transport and the protocol test canonicalization with json.dumps defaults that permit NaN/Infinity. branch_report.schema.json leaves task_ledger/test_ledger array items unconstrained. Therefore an otherwise-valid report can carry a Python non-finite float in one of those ledgers, serialize as the non-RFC JSON token NaN/Infinity, be reparsed by Python, preserve PRETTY_SORTED_UTF8_JSON_V1 byte equality, and admit a canonical HMAC-2 proof under the same implementation. The frozen transport layer therefore does not fail closed on non-standard JSON and is parser-dependent.
issue_ledger.next_action: Freeze the smallest protocol-2.5 parser/serializer hardening and regression before any clean countable credit; if accepted as authoritative, supersede this Gen11 control cohort rather than retrofitting frozen bytes.
issue_ledger.proposed_protocol_2_5_fix_test: Reject non-finite numbers recursively before HMAC/transport; call json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False) for both compact HMAC canonicalization and pretty committed transport; parse committed reports with parse_constant that raises on NaN/Infinity/-Infinity. Freeze a negative regression that injects each sentinel into an otherwise-valid unrestricted ledger field and requires schema/transport admission to fail closed.
issue_ledger.required_test: For each of NaN, Infinity and -Infinity, mutate only one otherwise-valid task_ledger/test_ledger value; signing/serialization/structural validation must reject the report before write/admission. A finite control report must still pass.
